s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent painful skin lesions with ulceration and systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Painful pimple-like bumps on bilateral lower legs
Ulcers with central eschars and dusky gray borders
key_facts: Patient is a young black woman
Presented with chills and bilateral lower extremity swelling
Recent course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus
Medical history includes treatment with methimazole and atenolol
Laboratory tests show elevated CRP and ESR
Normal C3 and C4 complement levels
ANA titer 1:80
P-ANCA titer 1:20
Anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO) titer 141 U
Anti-SSA/Ro antibodies level 120 U
Punch biopsy shows mid- and deep dermal lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with neutrophils and focal abscess
Second biopsy shows intraepidermal and dermal perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate with necrosis of vessel walls

salient_findings: Painful pimple-like bumps on bilateral lower legs

key_facts: Patient is a young black woman
Presented with chills and bilateral lower extremity swelling

Normal C3 and C4 complement levels

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CRP, ESR, and ANCA titer, consistent with systemic vasculitis

shortlist.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated ANCA titer and presence of necrotizing vasculitis on biopsy

shortlist.label: Cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of leukocytoclastic vasculitis on biopsy and skin lesions

shortlist.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic inflammation and necrotizing vasculitis on biopsy

shortlist.label: Erythema induratum
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with ulceration and systemic inflammation

shortlist.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent painful skin lesions with ulceration

shortlist.label: Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated ANCA titer and presence of systemic vasculitis

shortlist.label: Churg-Strauss syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated ESR, ANCA titer, and presence of systemic vasculitis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with painful lesions, chills, and bilateral lower extremity swelling, along with laboratory tests showing elevated CRP and ESR, normal C3 and C4 complement levels, and positive P-ANCA and anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO) titers, is consistent with microscopic polyangiitis. The punch biopsy findings of mid- and deep dermal lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with neutrophils and focal abscess, and the second biopsy showing intraepidermal and dermal perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate with necrosis of vessel walls, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: The absence of granulomas in the biopsy specimens makes this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: The presence of systemic symptoms such as chills and bilateral lower extremity swelling suggests a more systemic disease process

rejected.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
rejected.why: The lack of medium-sized artery involvement on biopsy makes this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Erythema induratum
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not match this condition

rejected.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: The presence of systemic symptoms and positive ANCA titers makes this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes microscopic polyangiitis, but microscopic polyangiitis is a more specific diagnosis

rejected.label: Churg-Strauss syndrome
rejected.why: The lack of asthma and eosinophilia makes this diagnosis less likely
